1.1: The Lord came to Jonah, son of Amittai, and was like,
1.2: "Get up and go to Nineveh—that big ol' city—and tell them folks they wildin'. Their mess done reached Me."
1.3: But what Jonah do? He said, "Nah, I'm good." Tried to dip out on God—ran the opposite way to Tarshish. He went down to Joppa, found a ship headin' that way, paid his lil' fare, and hopped on board. Thought he could duck God like that.
1.4: But God ain't playin'. He sent a violent storm on that water. Wind whippin'. Waves crashin'. That ship was about to snap in two.
1.5: The sailors? Terrified. Screamin' out to every god they knew. Start throwin' stuff off the boat just to keep it afloat. And where was Jonah? Knocked out. Sleepin' like he ain't got a care in the world—in the bottom of the ship.
1.6: The captain came down like, "Yo! How you sleepin' through this? Get up! Say somethin' to your God! We tryna live out here!"
1.7: The crew said, "Let's cast lots. Somebody's bringin' this bad luck." They cast lots and boom—it's Jonah.
1.8: They pressed him: "Bruh, what did you do?! Who are you?! Where you from?! What's your job?! What kinda trouble are you bringin' us?!"
1.9: Jonah said, "I'm Hebrew. I serve the Lord—the God that made the sea and the land."
1.10: The men got extra scared now. "You ran from that God?! Are you serious right now?!"
1.11: They like, "What we gotta do to make this sea chill out?"
1.12: Jonah said, "Throw me overboard. The storm's my fault. If I go, the sea'll calm down."
1.13: But the crew was tryna spare him. They rowed with everything they had, tryin' to get back to land. Didn't work. That storm just got louder.
1.14: So they prayed, "Lord, don't let us die 'cause of him. Don't blame us for this—we just doin' what we gotta do."
1.15: Then they picked Jonah up... And tossed him into the sea. Immediately—calm. Like the storm clocked out.
1.16: Them men were shook and amazed. They gave sacrifices to the Lord right then and there and made vows. God got their respect real quick.
1.17: Meanwhile, God already had a giant fish lined up. Soon as Jonah hit the water—chomp. That fish swallowed him whole. And Jonah sat in that fish belly for three whole days and three whole nights.

2.1: From inside that big ol' fish, Jonah finally came to his senses. He prayed to the Lord his God.
2.2: He said: "I cried out to the Lord 'cause I was goin' through it— And guess what? He still answered me. From the depths of hell itself, I called on You, And You heard me loud and clear.
2.3: "You the one who threw me out here, deep in the sea, Right in the middle where the waves crash heavy. All Your waters—just rollin' over me.
2.4: "I thought You had cut me off for good. But I kept my eyes on You. Still turned toward Your holy place, hopin' You'd see me.
2.5: "I was drownin'—like, soul-level drownin'. The deep wrapped me up tight. Seaweed was clingin' to my head like a crown of regret.
2.6: "I sank way down—like, to the roots of the mountains type deep. Felt like the earth shut the door behind me. But You, Lord my God, You brought me back up from all that darkness.
2.7: "When I had nothin' left, when my soul was weak and done, I remembered You, Lord. My prayer made it to You—straight into Your heavenly home.
2.8: "Folks who chase after fake gods? They turn their back on real mercy.
2.9: "But me? I'ma thank You for real. I'ma keep my word this time. 'Cause salvation only come from the Lord. Period."
2.10: Then God gave the fish the signal— And that fish spit Jonah out on dry land like, "I'm done with him."

3.1: God wasn't done with Jonah. He pulled up on him again, like, "Alright, let's try this one more time..."
3.2: "Get up. Go to Nineveh—that big ol' city—and this time, say exactly what I tell you to say."
3.3: So Jonah got up and actually did what God said this time. He made his way to Nineveh, a massive city—it would take three days just to walk across it.
3.4: On day one, Jonah started shoutin' in the streets: "In forty days, Nineveh gon' get wrecked!" That was the whole sermon. No mic. No slides. Just heat.
3.5: The folks in Nineveh actually listened. They believed what God said, called a fast, and put on sackcloth—from the bougie to the broke.
3.6: Word got to the king. He got off his throne, took off his royal fit, put on sackcloth, and sat down in ashes.
3.7: Then the king dropped a decree: "Don't let nobody eat—not even the animals. Cows, goats, folks—everybody fasting. Put sackcloth on the pets too! Cry out to God with all you got. Stop the wild behavior. Drop the violence. Fix it now."
3.8: "Everybody turn from your evil ways and the violence y'all been doin'. Get right!"
3.9: "Who knows? Maybe God will ease up. Maybe He won't go off on us like we deserve."
3.10: And guess what? God saw it. He saw how they changed up—for real. So He hit pause on the punishment. Didn't go through with the destruction He said was coming.

4.1: But Jonah? Man, he was heated. God showin' mercy had him mad for real.
4.2: He prayed, but it was more like a rant: "See Lord, this what I was talkin' 'bout back when I was still at home! This why I tried to dip to Tarshish in the first place. 'Cause I know You— You merciful. You patient. You full of love. You stay givin' folks a second chance. You always pull back when You could go off."
4.3: "So just go 'head and take me out, Lord. I'd rather die than watch this play out like I knew it would."
4.4: And the Lord was like, "So you mad… and you think that's okay?"
4.5: Jonah left the city, sat out east, and made himself a little spot— posted up in the shade, just waiting to see if Nineveh would still get clapped. (He was still hoping for fireworks.)
4.6: So God, being God, grew a big leafy plant right over Jonah. It gave him some good shade and cooled him down. Jonah was so happy about that plant. Had him feelin' blessed again.
4.7: But the next morning? God sent a worm. That worm ate that plant up. Gone.
4.8: Then God turned up the heat—literally. A hot east wind came through, and the sun was beatin' Jonah's head. He was weak, sweatin', miserable. He said, "Man, I'd rather die than live like this."
4.9: Then God asked again, "So you mad about the plant now?" Jonah said, "YES. Mad enough to die!"
4.10: And God hit him with a lesson: "You out here pressed over a plant. You ain't plant it, you ain't water it— it showed up in a night and disappeared just as quick.
4.11: And you mad over that, but I'm not supposed to care about Nineveh? A whole city with over 120,000 people who don't know up from down— plus all the animals?"
